transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I don’t care about the projects and hobbies I used to love anymore; nothing feels interesting to me now. I used to get so excited about tinkering with solar setups, painting, and going hiking, but lately, I just can't find any spark or joy in any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

This has been going on for a little over a year now. It really started when I lost a major solar contract to a bigger competitor, which left me with outstanding equipment loans and constant financial stress.
Have you ever experienced similar periods of feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things in the past, or is this the first time you've felt this way?
No, I haven't really experienced anything like this before. This is the first time in my life that I've felt so completely overwhelmed and down.
Along with losing interest in your hobbies, have you noticed other changes like trouble sleeping, low energy, or changes in your appetite during this past year?

Yes, both have been really bad. I lie awake for hours worrying about bills and then wake up at three or four in the morning unable to fall back asleep, and I also have to force myself to eat because food just tastes like cardboard now.
During this difficult year, have you found yourself struggling with feelings of worthlessness, or blaming yourself excessively for the financial situation?

Yes, absolutely. I keep telling myself I'm a complete screwup for letting the business stall and that I've wasted all these years. I feel like I don't even deserve to own a home or have nice things when I can't even keep up with my bills or return phone calls on time.
With all this heavy stress and self-blame over the past year, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or felt like life is no longer worth living?

On the really bad nights, when I'm staring at the stack of overdue bills, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. I've even pictured crashing my truck on the highway sometimes. But I want to be clear that I haven't made any actual plans to do anything like that.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt the exact opposite—with unusually high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling like your thoughts were racing?

No, I have never experienced periods of unusually high energy, decreased need for sleep, or racing thoughts like that. My struggle has been quite the opposite, where I just feel completely drained, heavy, and slowed down.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus on your work, or make everyday decisions lately?

Yes, concentrating and making decisions has become incredibly difficult lately. I find myself reading the same email or equipment spec sheet three or four times just to understand it, and even simple choices like what to cook or which invoice to handle first can leave me completely frozen.
To help me understand your overall health, have you been using alcohol or drugs to cope with this stress, or do you have any medical conditions like thyroid issues?
No, I don't really use alcohol or drugs to cope with the stress. And as far as I know, I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode (F32.2) lasting for over a year, triggered by a major business loss and financial stress. He exhibits all three key depressive symptoms (depressed mood, anhedonia, and severe fatigue/low energy) along with five additional symptoms (severe initial and late insomnia, marked appetite loss, intense feelings of worthlessness and guilt, severe concentration and decision-making difficulties, and suicidal ideation with visualization of self-harm). The high symptom count (8 out of 10), the presence of suicidal ideation, and the severe functional impairment (e.g., getting 'completely frozen' by simple daily decisions) warrant a diagnosis of a severe depressive episode rather than a moderate one (F32.1).
